58305-miss-nume-of-japan-a-japanese-amer.title: A Japanese-American Romance
58305-miss-nume-of-japan-a-japanese-amer.creator: Onoto Watanna
58305-miss-nume-of-japan-a-japanese-amer.description: A book by Onoto Watanna. Her art is the grace of the wild vine, under no obligation to a gardener, but with a charm that the gardener could not impart. A monogram wrought by nature's accident upon the golden leaf of autumn, does not belong to the world of letters, but it inspires more feeling and more poetry than a library squeezed out of man's tired brain. And this book is not unlike an autumn leaf blown from a forest in Japan. CHICAGO, January, 1899.

arxiv-1510-08092.title: Can 3D light localization be reached in “white paint”?
arxiv-1510-08092.creator: Tilo Sperling, Lukas Schertel, Mirco Ackermann, Geoffroy J. Aubry, Christof M. Aegerter, Georg Maret
arxiv-1510-08092.description: Abstract When waves scatter multiple times in 3D random media, a disorder driven phase transition from diffusion to localization may occur Anderson1958 ; Abrahams1979 . In “ The question of classical localization: A theory of white paint? ” P.W.Anderson suggested the possibility to observe light localization in TiO 2 samples Anderson1985 .

arxiv-2109-01131.title: Some model theory of Th ⁡ ( ℕ , ⋅ ) \operatorname{Th}(\mathbb{N},\cdot)
arxiv-2109-01131.creator: Atticus Stonestrom
arxiv-2109-01131.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Atticus Stonestrom. ‘Skolem arithmetic’ is the complete theory T T of the multiplicative monoid ( ℕ , ⋅ ) (\mathbb{N},\cdot) . We give a full characterization of the ∅ \varnothing -definable stably embedded sets of T T , showing in particular that, up to the relation of having the same definable closure, there is only one non-trivial one: the set of squarefree elements. We then prove that T T has weak elimination of imaginaries but not elimination of finite imaginaries.

arxiv-2405-04216.title: DESI 2024: Reconstructing Dark Energy using Crossing Statistics with DESI DR1 BAO data
arxiv-2405-04216.creator: R. Calderon, K. Lodha, A. Shafieloo, E. Linder, W. Sohn, A. de Mattia, J. L. Cervantes-Cota, R. Crittenden, T. M. Davis, M. Ishak, A. G. Kim, W. Matthewson, G. Niz, S. Park, J. Aguilar, S. Ahlen, S. Allen, D. Brooks, T. Claybaugh, A. de la Macorra, A. Dey, B. Dey, P. Doel, J. E. Forero-Romero, E. Ga
arxiv-2405-04216.description: Abstract We implement Crossing Statistics to reconstruct in a model-agnostic manner the expansion history of the universe and properties of dark energy, using DESI Data Release 1 (DR1) BAO data in combination with one of three different supernova compilations (PantheonPlus, Union3, and DES-SN5YR) and Planck CMB observations.

arxiv-2408-17103.title: Understanding the User: An Intent-Based Ranking Dataset
arxiv-2408-17103.creator: Abhijit Anand, Jurek Leonhardt, Venktesh V, Avishek Anand
arxiv-2408-17103.description: Abstract . As information retrieval systems continue to evolve, accurate evaluation and benchmarking of these systems become pivotal. Web search datasets, such as MS MARCO , primarily provide short keyword queries without accompanying intent or descriptions, posing a challenge in comprehending the underlying information need.

arxiv-2409-06070.title: A robust fourth-order finite-difference discretization for the strongly anisotropic transport equation in magnetized plasmas
arxiv-2409-06070.creator: L. Chacón, Jason Hamilton, Natalia Krasheninnikova
arxiv-2409-06070.description: Abstract We propose a second-order temporally implicit, fourth-order-accurate spatial discretization scheme for the strongly anisotropic heat transport equation characteristic of hot, fusion-grade plasmas. Following [Du Toit et al., Comp. Phys. Comm ., 228 (2018)], the scheme transforms mixed-derivative diffusion fluxes (which are responsible for the lack of a discrete maximum principle) into nonlinear advective fluxes, amenable to nonlinear-solver-friendly monotonicity-preserving limiters.

arxiv-2409-15900.title: Speeding up quantum annealing with engineered dephasing
arxiv-2409-15900.creator: Mykolas Sveistrys, Josias Langbehn, Raphaël Menu, Steve Campbell, Giovanna Morigi, Christiane P. Koch
arxiv-2409-15900.description: Abstract Building on the insight that engineered noise, specifically, engineered dephasing can enhance the adiabaticity of controlled quantum dynamics, we investigate how a dephasing-generating coupling to an auxiliary quantum system affects quantum annealing protocols. By calculating the exact reduced system dynamics, we show how this coupling enhances the system’s adiabaticity solely through a coherent mechanism - an effective energy rescaling.

arxiv-2506-06832.title: Cross-Entropy Games for Language Models: From Implicit Knowledge to General Capability Measures
arxiv-2506-06832.creator: Clément Hongler ∗, Andrew Emil
arxiv-2506-06832.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Clément Hongler ∗, Andrew Emil. Large Language Models (LLMs) define probability measures on text. By considering the implicit knowledge question of what it means for an LLM to know such a measure and what it entails algorithmically, we are naturally led to formulate a series of tasks that go beyond generative sampling, involving forms of summarization, counterfactual thinking, anomaly detection, originality search, reverse prompting, debating, creative solving, etc.

arxiv-2506-15973.title: Short–Range Hard–Sphere Potential and Coulomb Interaction: Deser–Trueman Formula for Rydberg States of Exotic Atomic Systems
arxiv-2506-15973.creator: Gregory S. Adkins, Ulrich D. Jentschura
arxiv-2506-15973.description: Abstract In exotic atomic systems with hadronic constituent particles, it is notoriously difficult to estimate the strong-interaction correction to energy levels. It is well known that, due to the strength of the nuclear interaction, the problem cannot be treated on the basis of Wigner–Brioullin perturbation theory.

arxiv-2507-17620.title: Exterior Cyclic Polytopes and Convexity of Amplituhedra
arxiv-2507-17620.creator: Elia Mazzucchelli, Elizabeth Pratt
arxiv-2507-17620.description: Abstract The amplituhedron is a semialgebraic set in the Grassmannian. We study convexity and duality of amplituhedra. We introduce a notion of convexity, called extendable convexity , for real semialgebraic sets in any embedded projective variety. We show that the k = m = 2 k=m=2 amplituhedron is extendably convex in the Grassmannian of lines in projective three-space.

arxiv-2512-10744.title: Exploring New Propagation Scales With Galactic Neutrinos
arxiv-2512-10744.creator: Miller MacDonald, Kiara Carloni, Carlos A. Argüelles, Ivan Martínez-Soler, Rafael Alves Batista
arxiv-2512-10744.description: Abstract The recent observation of high-energy Galactic neutrinos by IceCube allows for searches of new physics affecting neutrino propagation on scales of 𝒪 ⁡ ( 10 9 − 10 15 ) ​ km / GeV \mathcal{O}(10^{9}-10^{15})\,\mathrm{km/GeV} in distance over energy. We assess the sensitivity of upcoming measurements of Galactic neutrinos by IceCube and KM3NeT to such new phenomena.

arxiv-2601-17948.title: Tensor form factors of decuplet hyperons in QCD
arxiv-2601-17948.creator: Z. Asmaee 1, K. Azizi 1,2
arxiv-2601-17948.description: Abstract Tensor form factors encode essential information about the internal spin structure and tensor dynamics of baryons. In this work, we investigate the tensor form factors of the baryon hyperons Ω − \Omega^{-} , Σ ∗ ⁣ + \Sigma^{*+} , and Ξ ∗ ⁣ − \Xi^{*-} within the framework of QCD sum rules.

pmc-10625517.title: Anti-oomycete activities from essential oils and their major compounds on Phytophthora infestans
pmc-10625517.creator: Caroline Deweer, Karin Sahmer, Jérôme Muchembled
pmc-10625517.description: Botanicals are various plant-based products like plant extracts or essential oils. Anti-fungal activities of selected essential oils were tested on the pathogen causing potato and tomato late blight (Phytophthora infestans). Tests to evaluate anti-oomycete activities of commercial essential oils and their major compounds were carried out in vitro in microplate in liquid media.

pmc-10648718.title: Transmembrane Helices 7 and 8 Confer Aggregation Sensitivity to the Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Conductance Regulator
pmc-10648718.creator: Bertrand Kleizen, Eduardo de Mattos, Olga Papaioannou, Michele Monti, Gian Gaetano Tartaglia, Peter van der Sluijs, Ineke Braakman, Mauro Salvi
pmc-10648718.description: The Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Conductance Regulator (CFTR) is a large multi-spanning membrane protein that is susceptible to misfolding and aggregation. We have identified here the region responsible for this instability. Temperature-induced aggregation of C-terminally truncated versions of CFTR demonstrated that all truncations up to the second transmembrane domain (TMD2), including the R region, largely resisted aggregation.

pmc-11458547.title: Role of nucleobase-specific interactions in the binding and bending of DNA by human male sex determination factor SRY
pmc-11458547.creator: Joseph D Racca, Yen-Shan Chen, Adam R Brabender, Umberto Battistin, Michael A Weiss, Millie M Georgiadis
pmc-11458547.description: Y-chromosome–encoded master transcription factor SRY functions in the embryogenesis of therian mammals to initiate male development. Through interactions of its conserved high-mobility group box within a widened DNA minor groove, SRY and related Sox factors induce sharp bends at specific DNA target sites.

pmc-11496321.title: Health-related quality of life and supportive care needs in young adult cancer survivors—a longitudinal population-based study
pmc-11496321.creator: Alexandra Wide, Johan Ahlgren, Karin E Smedby, Kristina Hellman, Roger Henriksson, Olof Ståhl, Claudia Lampic, Lena Wettergren
pmc-11496321.description: PurposeTo examine health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and supportive care needs among young adult (YA) cancer survivors up to 3 years post-diagnosis.MethodsA national cohort of individuals diagnosed at 18–39 years with breast, cervical, ovarian, or testicular cancer, lymphoma or brain tumor was approached with surveys at 1.5 (n = 1010, response rate 67%) and 3 (n = 722) years post-diagnosis.

pmc-12496506.title: Salvage coiling after the inadvertent proximal migration of a neuroform atlas stent into middle cerebral artery aneurysms: A report of two cases
pmc-12496506.creator: Jinlu Yu
pmc-12496506.description: Introduction and importanceDuring endovascular treatment (EVT) of middle cerebral artery (MCA) aneurysms using a Neuroform Atlas stent (NAS), inadvertent proximal migration of the NAS into the aneurysm may occur.Case presentationsPatient 1 was a 49-year-old female with an unruptured MCA bifurcation aneurysm.

pmc-12622594.title: Causal relationship between plasma homocysteine levels and colorectal cancer: A Mendelian randomization study
pmc-12622594.creator: Xiaosong Ru, Linjun Wu, Yong Guo, Yinfeng Shen
pmc-12622594.description: Given that homocysteine (Hey) may be a viable target for intervention and that there is uncertainty regarding the causal relationship between plasma Hcy levels and colorectal cancer (CRC), this study used Mendelian randomization (MR) to investigate the relationship between Hey and CRC.

pmc-12780409.title: Impacting factors of diagnostic accuracy of ultrasound-guided percutaneous core needle biopsy in mediastinal lesions: an analysis with 622 cases
pmc-12780409.creator: Chang-Lu Wang, Wen-Yue Cao, Teng Mao, Lei Zhu, Jie Chen, Lei Wang
pmc-12780409.description: BackgroundUltrasound-guided percutaneous core needle biopsy (UGNB) has been widely adopted in pre-treatment pathological diagnosis in mediastinal neoplasms, while the accuracy rates varied in previous reports. We analyzed the impacting factors of accuracy in this retrospective study, aiming to further improve the diagnostic yield.

pmc-13019955.title: Use of pedicled thigh flaps for complex abdominal wall reconstruction: A case series
pmc-13019955.creator: Reece Hefner, Anirudh Kulkarni, Hakan Guven, John B. Park, Margaret Dalena, Alekha Kolli, Richard L. Agag, Jeremy C. Sinkin
pmc-13019955.description: Complex abdominal wall defects that result from oncologic resection, infection, or trauma often require advanced reconstructive techniques beyond primary fascial closure or mesh reinforcement alone. In cases where primary closure is not feasible due to extensive tissue loss, pedicled thigh-based flaps offer a robust, vascularized solution to restore abdominal wall integrity.

pmc-13085907.title: The overexpression of HOXC6 in LUSC and pan-squamous cell carcinomas indicates the coexistence of nuclear division regulatory mechanisms
pmc-13085907.creator: Shu-Jia He, Ke-Jun Wu, Yi-Yang Chen, Yan-Ting Zhan, Yu-Xing Tang, Xiao-Song Chen, Zhi-Guang Huang, Qi Li, Bin Li, Yong-Yao Gu, Gang Chen, Jin-Liang Kong, Feng Chen
pmc-13085907.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundHomeobox C6 (HOXC6) shows abnormal expression in various tumors, but its pattern in lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) remains unclear.ObjectiveTo investigate HOXC6's expression and function in LUSC.MethodsHOXC6 expression was analyzed using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) in LUSC, cervical squamous cell carcinoma (CESC), esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC), and oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), verified by RNA-seq and immunohistochemistry (IHC). CRISPR knockdown assessed proliferation impact.

pmc-13344431.title: SARS-CoV-2 testing uptake and its determinants in six ethnic groups living in Amsterdam, the Netherlands: a registry-based study within the HELIUS cohort
pmc-13344431.creator: Sophie L Campman, Anders Boyd, Nina van Wilgen, Felix P Chilunga, Liza Coyer, Janke Schinkel, Charles Agyemang, Henrike Galenkamp, Anitra D M Koopman, Jelle Koopsen, Matthijs Welkers, Karien Stronks, Maria Prins
pmc-13344431.description: Diagnostic testing was key in preventing transmission of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) in the pre-vaccination era of the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic. This study compared SARS-CoV-2 polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing uptake and its determinants across six ethnic groups in Amsterdam, the Netherlands.

pmc-13433883.title: Rapamycin‐nanoliposomes target the mTORC1‐mediated autophagy–lysosomal and NLRP3/Caspase‐1 pathways to inhibit nucleus pulposus cell senescence in intervertebral discs
pmc-13433883.creator: Hui Xing, Miao Yu, Jiabin Liu, Runzhi Zhao, Xuezheng Ai, Rong Tang, Tong Zhu, Yuqing Li, Lu Jiang, Quanfang Wei, Youying Huang, Yu Guo, Tao Jiang, Bo Huang
pmc-13433883.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Nucleus pulposus (NP) cell quiescence maintains intervertebral disc homeostasis, while mTORC1 regulates autophagy–lysosomal function and inflammatory secretion to preserve quiescence—rapamycin specifically targets mTORC1. Herein, we fabricated rapamycin‐nanoliposomes (rapa‐lipos) via ultrasonic dispersion, thin‐film dispersion, and filtration to improve rapamycin bioavailability, investigating their role in inhibiting the senescence phenotype of NP cells through β‐gal staining, lysosomal staining, transmission electron microscopy, ELISA, and cell cycle inhibitors.
